comment: This class teaches you to analyze and write the way Dr. Pappas wants you to. However, she is willing to meet to answer questions and offers feedback and revisions on assignments. The texts we read were pretty difficult, but we discussed them at length in class so I was never confused about them. She is a tough grader, especially about grammar.

Some like her, some don't. Extremely smart and qualified, clearly thinks she's better than everyone else. Interesting FYS, but she makes it boring and repetitive. If you want to write abstract essays that have no connection (comparing postcards to books) this class is for you. Her feedback is the same every time and you will never get above an 88.

Dr. Pappas taught me writing lessons that I will take with me throughout the rest of my academic career. Her lectures are engaging and she uses a lot of multimedia to supplement each class. There is quite a bit of reading, but the group discussions during class help a lot. She is a strict grader but her comments will help you exponentially.

The image analysis and writing tips taught in this class are such that you'll wonder if you're not back in sixth grade, but an A-grade paper would be nigh impossible even for someone who flew through an upper level English course just the semester before. This FYS doesn't teach you how to write for college, but for Dr. Pappas specifically.

For an FYS class, it is more work than usual. A lot of readings but not too many papers. If you are a good writer and enjoy the content of the class then you should take the class for sure, but if you aren't a great writer and don't have an interest in Paris then there's no reason for you to take the class.

I think the Double Life of Paris is one of the more interesting FYSs, and compared to many others it doesn't have that much work. However, Dr Pappas is a very tough grader and that greatly impacted my enjoyment of the class. I felt the grading was especially tough for a first semester FYS.

Good FYS if you need one. Dr. Pappas is very knowledgeable about Paris and France and general, and I thought most of the material was interesting. The grading of papers can feel kind of harsh sometimes, as it feels like she wants things done in a specific way. But, she gives lots of specific feedback so it somewhat balances out.

Prof. Pappas was very nice and generous do to the circumstances of the semester. Her teaching style and feedback is not clear. She made PowerPoints with the wrong way and then the right way to do something. It felt like we were not learning just merely memorizing the way she wanted us to write. Again, very nice professor and patient with students.

Class gets repetitive and boring. She doesn't had out much hw, but she does her grading outline is unclear. Her feedback on assignments can also be confusing. Pretty much a toss up here, so if you're stuck with class, take it and deal with it.

Professor Pappas was an absolutely fantastic professor for my FYS. She found a way to make class interesting and exciting every day, and was always free to talk. We watched great films, and read great books, both of which were always followed up by even better discussions. You need to participate in class, but if you do, the class will be great.

This FYS was pretty easy, the readings usually werent long and on the few assignments we had she was not a tough grader. Big emphasis on participation but not hard to do, lots of opportunity to talk. Not always super clear when explaining things but will try to help you outside of class.

Not sure why this course is called 'writing boot camp.' We had a few larger writing assignments, but nothing to get too worried about. Professor Pappas seemed to be a pretty tough grader, but with the extra credit and frequent participation, you should be okay! Analyzing the difficult French poems, plays, etc. makes you feel pretty intelligent;)
Very nice prof. Always willing to help/talk. Lots of reading and writing. Loves to talk politics.

Dr Pappas is the best for FYS. Very manageable work load.... not too much, but not too little. You will leave the class feeling like you learned a lot. Beyond that, she is a very nice person and knows her material well.

Dr. Pappas is great. She makes class fun, even though it's a "bootcamp" for upper-level French courses. Participation is a big deal, so you'll definitely improve on your speaking skills in French 305! Also, she is a bit of a tough grader who is very specific with what she is looking for, so be prepared to work extra hard to get a good grade.

I took Pappas for my FYS- she was super nice and there wasn't too much work. She's kind of a tough grader- I've never gotten anything over a 90 in the class, and there aren't that many assignments. She is super tough when it comes to participation, and you only get 2 absences before they start affecting your grade.

Eh, she is nice, the class was alright, I learned a bit. Nothing great though, her selection of movies could have been better. I think I would have learned more with another teacher. Not much of a push to succeed.

Pappas is not a horrible person, but she really likes to critique students and she demands insane effort. she responds to a lot of people in class just by saying 'no' and moving on, but I think my French did improve. she grades papers very hard and you really have to speak up in class to get a good participation grade.
A lot more laid back than you'd expect. I liked her enough. Average grader, not a lot of work.

She's a very nice and funny teacher. Her class is pretty interesting and she keep it moving. The quizzes and presentations are all pretty easy and manageable. The homework is mainly exercises from the book and the movie labs are optional but if you do miss it, you're expected to watch it in your own time. Grading wise, she's consistent and relatively easy

Pappas is honestly a great teacher. She knows a lot about French and is very cheerful and funny. She likes to tell students about her stories and things that have amazed her. But she can be strict and is very by the book. Taking her is not a bad idea. People either love of hate her and I don't hate her.

She has favorites, & isn't shy about showing it. She spent the majority of her time chatting w/students who were already proficient, instead of helping other students actually learn. It felt like she decided my grade the 3rd day of class, & no amount of work, study, or talking to her was going to change that. Not recommended.
Prof Pappas rocks! Any negative coments are from students who don't do their work and are just lazy. She is extremely helpful and knows her stuff. If you want to LEARN something, take her class.
Really nice teacher for CORE. Love the class discussions. The only downside is that she's a bit hard on grading papers.

Just an incredibly hard grader on papers. Good class discussions, but paper topics are very hard because she likes comparing books that have nothing in common. Overall good person, just expects too much from her students.
A great professor, always clear and willing to help. She is even tolerant of the people who pretty obviously are not doing the work.
The class was very lightweight.  Pappas apparently doesn't have much confidence in her students, or just doesn't care.

Prof. Pappas is the best prof EVERRRR.  she is very pretty and loves her job :-) don't talk badly about her just because you may not have done well in her class.  she is smart, friendly, and very helpful go to her if you need help she is very cultured and knows more than you think!
BORING!
If you hate her class, you're probably not doing your work, nver speaking, and therefore getting a D. Why dont you blame yourself instead of the class?
I love this class. Her comments on compositions are very helpful. She is always willing to help. Very nice and always positive. Way to go Prof. Pappas!!!!
I hate this class.
you people are crazy. she doesnt play favorites! her favorite is anybody who works hard. and she's opoen to any political views in her classroom

Way to go Pr. Papps, first you need to respect the students and then stand in front of the class and pretend to be impartial. She has her favotites and is not ashamed to show that. Too subjective and unclear in her assignments. Avoid her any time you can.
Pappas is great.  Ignore the right-wing wackos who can't take a genuine and nuanced political discussion.  She makes you think, and think hard.  Worth the work!

One of the best teachers I have had at Richmond. Her classes are never the same because she always has something interesting to say! Definitley take a class with her. just watch out for political discussions if you are a conservative.

Hates.  Unless you love French culture and language, you will despise this class and the professor.  Having it 5 days a week doesn't help either. Exams are extremely difficult and she is not very helpful when you go to see her during office hours. If you haven't had intense French in the past, this will be a struggle.  She's also extremely liberal.
worst teacher i've had at richmond

Pappas is hard and takes pride in making tests as hard as she can.  Word has it she enjoys bragging to other prof.'s about her impossible book-like exams.  If you just want the gen-ed requirement, DO NOT GO PAPPAS!
I love Pappas, she's the best!

Prof Pappas is a great teacher.  She makes class really fun and interesting by taking things beyond the book.  She encourages conversation and discussin.  She is really understanding about work load and her assignments aren't too bad.  Overall, she just creates a really fun classroom atmosphere.
Shes really good about moving assignments, etc (and she didn't make us do all of contextes) but she's very demanding and definitely had favorites in the class.

Professor Pappas Rocks. She challenges you to think beyond the texts, to understand the big picture. She goes out of her way to help everyone learn, but won't do the learning for you. She it tough, but fair. If you don't do the work, you (like ABBA) will be singing "Waterloo..."

She doesn't make you do all of contextes, which is good, but she grades very tough.  Her Prose class is very interesting, mostly discussion based, and her assignments are reasonable.  Also ... don't start a polticial discussion with her unless you are very liberal.
